headline: Govt decides in principle to relocate Secretariat to Agargaon
summary: The move to the former trade fair ground will be finalized by the cabinet after preparatory work by the Planning Commission and Ministry of Housing.
details: The government has decided in principle to relocate the Secretariat to the former trade fair ground in Dhaka's Agargaon, according to Housing and Public Works Minister Zakaria Taher.
The decision was reached during a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman last Wednesday.
While the decision is currently in principle, the final approval will be granted by the cabinet.
The proposal to move the Secretariat to Agargaon had been discussed several times during the previous Awami League government's tenure but was never implemented.
Policymakers in the Prime Minister's Office are now keen to begin work on the project during the current government's tenure.
The Planning Commission and the Ministry of Housing and Public Works have already started preparatory work.
A preliminary decision has been reached on one of three designs submitted by the Department of Architecture for the new complex.
Once the cabinet gives final approval, activities relating to the project are expected to accelerate.
caption:
The Bangladesh Secretariat is set for a major move. The government has decided in principle to relocate it to Agargaon.

The government has decided in principle to relocate the Secretariat to the former trade fair ground in Dhaka's Agargaon, according to Housing and Public Works Minister Zakaria Taher.

The decision was reached during a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman last Wednesday.

While the decision is currently in principle, the final approval will be granted by the cabinet.

The proposal to move the Secretariat to Agargaon had been discussed several times during the previous Awami League government's tenure but was never implemented.

Policymakers in the Prime Minister's Office are now keen to begin work on the project during the current government's tenure.

The Planning Commission and the Ministry of Housing and Public Works have already started preparatory work.

A preliminary decision has been reached on one of three designs submitted by the Department of Architecture for the new complex.

Once the cabinet gives final approval, activities relating to the project are expected to accelerate.

headline_marked: Bangladesh's [[foreign debt hits record $114.98 billion]] as public liabilities surge
headline: Bangladesh's foreign debt hits record $114.98 billion as public liabilities surge
summary: External debt rose by nearly $4 billion in just three months, reaching a total equivalent to approximately Tk 14.17 trillion.
details: Bangladesh's total external debt has climbed to a record $114.98 billion, according to figures released by the Bangladesh Bank on Sunday. This represents a 3.65 percent increase from $110.93 billion at the end of March.
The surge was primarily driven by public-sector external debt, which rose from $90.91 billion in March to $95.10 billion in June—an increase of about $4.2 billion.
In contrast, private-sector debt saw a slight decline of $140 million, falling to $19.88 billion due to reductions in short-term borrowing, trade loans, and buyers' credit.
Long-term borrowing makes up the bulk of the debt, accounting for 87.52 percent of the total at $100.64 billion, while short-term debt stands at $14.35 billion.
The country owes $48.96 billion to multilateral development institutions like the World Bank and ADB, and $32.54 billion to bilateral creditors.
Other debts include $10.60 billion in commercial loans and $5.97 billion borrowed from the International Monetary Fund.
Historically, external debt stood at $20.65 billion when the caretaker government took office in 2007. It rose to $104.76 billion before the Awami League government was ousted in 2024.
Borrowing has continued under the current interim government, with the debt stock reaching $113.58 billion by the end of 2025.
caption:
Bangladesh's foreign debt has hit a record $114.98 billion, jumping nearly $4 billion in just three months.

Bangladesh's total external debt has climbed to a record $114.98 billion, according to figures released by the Bangladesh Bank on Sunday. This represents a 3.65 percent increase from $110.93 billion at the end of March.

The surge was primarily driven by public-sector external debt, which rose from $90.91 billion in March to $95.10 billion in June—an increase of about $4.2 billion.

In contrast, private-sector debt saw a slight decline of $140 million, falling to $19.88 billion due to reductions in short-term borrowing, trade loans, and buyers' credit.

Long-term borrowing makes up the bulk of the debt, accounting for 87.52 percent of the total at $100.64 billion, while short-term debt stands at $14.35 billion.

The country owes $48.96 billion to multilateral development institutions like the World Bank and ADB, and $32.54 billion to bilateral creditors.

Other debts include $10.60 billion in commercial loans and $5.97 billion borrowed from the International Monetary Fund.

Historically, external debt stood at $20.65 billion when the caretaker government took office in 2007. It rose to $104.76 billion before the Awami League government was ousted in 2024.

Borrowing has continued under the current interim government, with the debt stock reaching $113.58 billion by the end of 2025.
